consequence: Any LOSO comparison of two pipeline versions needs several draws per version and must compare distributions, not two single numbers. Historical single-draw LOSO comparisons in this project are weaker than they were presented as.
limitation: n=3 estimates the spread poorly. It is enough to show the comparison is underpowered; it is not enough to bound the variance or to rule a real stage B effect in or out.
method: Three demand builds under IDENTICAL code, differing only in --seed, each followed by a full six-fold LOSO on the same window (2025-09-16).
question: Can a single LOSO run distinguish a pipeline change from the randomness of one candidate-pool draw?
verdict: UNDERPOWERED. The spread between three draws of the SAME code is 0.418, the same order as the 0.566 shift previously attributed to stage B. A single LOSO run therefore cannot separate a pipeline change from draw noise at this magnitude, and the stage B claim is NOT established.
